description.narrative:
IGAD Centre of Excellence for Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (ICEPCVE) will implement an 18-month pilot project to Enhance Gender Sensitive Approaches among State and Non-State Actors to Prevent and Counter Violent Extremism (P/CVE) and Terrorism in East and Horn of Africa. The programme aims to contribute towards narrowing gender gaps and amplifying the voice of women and their contribution in P/CVE work in East and Horn of Africa. The project will target legislators, researchers, media practitioners, youth, CSOs and government officials from key ministries dealing with P/CVE. It is expected that the programme will contribute to 5 outcome areas:
Result 1: Gender sensitive P/CVE legislation and policies Result 2: Gender sensitive reporting Result 3: Gender sensitive criminal justice system Result 4: Gender sensitive counter and alternative messages Result 5: Gender sensitive research
The contribution is in line with Sida's regional strategy for Africa, as it provides support to one of the main regional actors, the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD), in mediation, peace and security in the Horn of Africa.

Avtalet med IGAD Center of Excellence for Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (ICEPCVE) avser ett pilotprojekt för att "stärka statliga och icke-statliga aktörers ansatser för att förebygga och motverka våldsam extremism (P/CVE) och terrorism utifrån ett genusperspektiv i Östra Afrika och på Afrikas Horn". Programmet syftar till att bidra till att minska könsskillnader och förstärka kvinnors röst och deras bidrag i P/CVE-arbetet. Programmet kommer att inriktas på lagstiftare, forskare, medieutövare, ungdomar, samhällsorganisationer och regeringstjänstemän från centrala ministerier som arbetar med P/CVE. Det förväntas att programmet kommer att bidra till rättsväsende, lagstiftning och policy, rapportering, mot- och alternativbudskap samt forskning kring P/CVE som är genuskänslig.

The agreement with IGAD Centre of Excellence for Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (ICEPCVE) is for a pilot project to “Enhance Gender Sensitive Approaches among State and Non-State Actors to Prevent and Counter Violent Extremism (P/CVE) and Terrorism in East and Horn of Africa”. The programme aims to contribute towards narrowing gender gaps and amplifying the voice of women and their contribution in P/CVE work in East and Horn of Africa. The programme will target legislators, researchers, media practitioners, youth, CSOs and government officials from key ministries dealing with P/CVE. It is expected that the programme will contribute to legislation and policies, criminal justice system, reporting; counter and alternative messages and research for P/CVE which are gender sensitive.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
In course of implementing the project, the Centre has trained a total of 160 men and women actively involved in preventing and countering violent extremism and terrorism in East and Horn of Africa on how to effectively integrate gender perspectives and conflict sensitivity in their work; of these, 71 are male and 89 are female which translates to 44% of males and 56% of females respectively. All the activities under the result areas: Gender Sensitive Legislations, Gender Sensitive Criminal Justice System, Gender Sensitive Reporting and Gender Sensitive Counter Messaging were successfully implemented within the stipulated timelines.
Following participation in the training, the participants indicated that they would share the information acquired with their workmates and some promised to plan short in-house sessions to cascade the insights gained to their colleagues. For instance, some of the activities were envisioned to contribute towards developing and augmented gender sensitive P/CVE legislations and policies. Following the three meetings held with legislators drawn from peace and security committees, commitments to initiate amends on existing P/CVE legislations and to develop draft P/CVE legislations where non-existent were made. In Uganda, the deputy speaker pledged to support the legislators in ensuring that the draft P/CVE strategy in place is validated and implemented accordingly. In Ethiopia, the legislators have initiated conversations on the need to have a P/CVE strategy in place and the Centre is in contact with them to provide support where necessary. In addition to the commitments made, at the last meeting held with the legislators provided an avenue to successfully form the IGAD parliamentary caucus network, the first in the entire institution which will be expected to champion peace, security, development, and integration in the region. These pledgees are expected to sustain the results.
The summative evaluation showed the evaluation found the program empowered participants to influence policies within their organizations, showing its integration with local and national policy frameworks. It created a sense of belonging through the establishment of professional networking platforms and indirectly influenced policy as respondents reporting amplified discussions on gender issues within the P/CVE arena. Furthermore, the development of policy papers and legislative initiatives, media pieces as well as the Vibrant engagements on social and mainstream media is expected to shape regional policies and frameworks related to gender and P/CVE.
